prompt.context: Our client, Loonilever, is a major consumer products company with operations in over 80 countries. Loonilever operates across all categories in the consumer products space — personal wash, hair care, oral care, laundry, household cleaning, skincare, etc. Over the last decade it has been losing share to its key competitor B&G, particularly in categories where B&G is strong. Loonilever is very keen on regaining or building share in key categories. Skincare is the most profitable category for large consumer products players, with gross margins of ~75% (vs. 30% for laundry). Loonilever is now evaluating an entry into China's skincare market, a market that B&G has enjoyed market leadership in for over a decade. Though Loonilever is the market leader in China's laundry segment, it does not currently operate in the skincare segment. Loonilever has hired McKinsey to help them determine what their potential entry strategy into the Chinese skincare market should be.
prompt.question: What should Loonilever's entry strategy into the Chinese skincare market be?

clarifying_info.q: What specific objective is Loonilever trying to achieve?
clarifying_info.a: Loonilever wants to achieve (a) revenue of $100 million in two years and (b) enter a market that displays significant potential for future growth.

clarifying_info.q: What market share does Loonilever believe it can achieve in the anti-ageing segment in year t+2?
clarifying_info.a: Provide whatever share figure the interviewer has specified — this detail should be provided proactively if the candidate asks.

framework: Industry analysis: size of market, segmentation, key players and market share, consumer/market trends within each segment
Revenue potential: volume projections by segment, pricing analysis

Other strategic factors: gateway to other Asian markets (SE Asia), potential as a global manufacturing hub, competitive disruption — by entering B&G's stronghold, Loonilever can force B&G to bleed/defend, potentially destabilizing their business model

questions.prompt: What is B&G's current market share in China's skincare market? If B&G maintains the status quo (same marketing expenditures, no dramatic new product launches), will its market share go up, go down, or stay constant in two years?
questions.guidance: A strong candidate will immediately note: (1) China's skincare market is large and growing — attractive. (2) B&G's high market share means Loonilever faces a tough competitive environment. B&G will defend aggressively given the category's high profitability. The math requires projecting market revenue and B&G revenue forward two years by segment, then recalculating B&G's share. The key insight is that B&G holds the largest share in a slow-growing sub-segment; as fast-growing segments (Anti-Ageing at 20%) become a larger share of the total market, B&G's overall share declines even if B&G grows in line with its own segments. Candidate should avoid the trap of saying 'no change in share since market and B&G are growing at the same rate.' After solving, a strong candidate will link the answer back to the main question by recommending entry into the Anti-Ageing segment.

math.setup: Part 1: Current B&G market share = B&G total revenue / total market revenue (sum across all segments). Part 2: Project each segment's total market revenue two years forward using segment-specific growth rates. Project B&G's revenue in each segment using the same growth rates (status quo assumption). Recalculate B&G's share in year t+2 = projected B&G total revenue / projected total market revenue.
steps: Sum current segment revenues to get total market size
Calculate current B&G share = B&G revenue / total market revenue
Apply segment growth rates to project year t+2 market size per segment and B&G revenue per segment
Sum projected figures to get t+2 totals
Observe that B&G share declines because the Anti-Ageing segment (where B&G has lower share) grows at 20% and becomes a larger fraction of the total market
math.answer: B&G's overall market share declines in two years because the high-growth Anti-Ageing segment dilutes B&G's aggregate share. Implication: Loonilever should target the Anti-Ageing segment — it is the fastest-growing, highest-margin (85%) segment, and Loonilever can capture $100M+ revenue there.

questions.prompt: What is the average price point in the Anti-Ageing (AA) market? What is the ideal AA price point for Loonilever to enter at? (Assume all other information from the earlier question still holds.)
questions.guidance: The average price point calculation should be straightforward from Exhibit 4 data (weighted average of top-end MNC price and local brand price by volume or revenue share). The second part tests business intuition — there is no single right answer, but the candidate must argue their choice logically. Three valid approaches: (1) Top end at $25/100gm — targets high-income urban consumers; highest margin (85%); but very competitive against well-resourced MNCs who will defend aggressively. (2) Bottom end at $5/100gm — lower margins (less concern since focus is revenue); commoditized market, local brands less marketing-savvy; requires strong distribution network (Loonilever has this via laundry leadership). (3) Middle ($10–$20/100gm) — space is largely unoccupied; leverages Loonilever's two strengths: marketing/branding and distribution; sacrifices some margin to build revenue; positions Loonilever as the 'bridge' upgrading mass consumers to premium; avoids direct cash burn against entrenched MNCs; could force MNCs to match lower price points and bleed. Bonus points for identifying solution 3 (middle-market bridge strategy).

math.setup: Weighted average price = (volume at top-end × $25 + volume at low-end × $5) / total volume. Exact volumes from Exhibit 4.
steps: Weight $25 and $5 price points by respective shares
math.answer: Average price visible from Exhibit 4 data; exact figure in exhibit_p112.png. The recommended entry point depends on strategic logic (see guidance above).

brainstorming.prompt: Are there strategic reasons for Loonilever to enter China's skincare market even if it cannot achieve the $100M revenue target?

categories.name: Geographic/Strategic Platform
ideas: China as a gateway to other high-growth SE Asian skincare markets
China as a potential global manufacturing hub for skincare products

categories.name: Competitive Disruption
ideas: Entering B&G's most profitable stronghold forces B&G to defend and spend, potentially destabilizing B&G's overall business model
Making B&G bleed in China could reduce B&G's resources to compete against Loonilever in other categories and geographies

categories.name: Category Learning
ideas: Building skincare capability in China develops IP, formulations, and marketing know-how transferable globally
Establishes relationships with Chinese retail channels and distributors

recommendation: Loonilever should enter China's skincare market in the Anti-Ageing segment, as it can meet the $100M revenue threshold in two years. The AA segment is growing at 20% per year and carries the highest gross margins (~85%), making it the most attractive entry point.

Loonilever should enter the AA segment at the middle price tier ($10–$20/100gm) — a largely unoccupied space — leveraging its existing marketing/branding strengths and its established distribution network (built through laundry market leadership). This avoids direct confrontation with deep-pocketed MNCs at the top end while building a meaningful revenue base.
risks: We have not modeled the impact of competitive response from major MNC players (B&G and others); they are unlikely to allow Loonilever a free run regardless of entry tier
Revenue projections are based on assumed market share capture; a sensitivity analysis should be conducted for different competitor response scenarios
Entering at the middle tier sacrifices the 85% top-end margin; profitability vs. revenue trade-off has not been fully assessed
next_steps: Conduct sensitivity analysis on revenue projections under different competitive response scenarios
Now that revenue potential is validated, analyze the cost structure and perform a break-even analysis to determine whether the AA market can be profitable for Loonilever long-term
Assess Loonilever's specific capability gaps (formulation, in-store expertise, beauty consultant training) required for the chosen tier
Develop detailed go-to-market plan: channel strategy, pricing, brand positioning, launch timeline
